svg.title: with the same two-sided density bounds. A physical gauge transformation g is lifted by rx 7→rxg−1 x with A fixed, so it does not move the density at all; a signed lattice permutation acts on both columns and preserves the product Haar prior and the raw action for the reasons just given. The local representatives used in the reflection argument and their finite products have exactly the same expectations before and after the lift. This is exact recovery of a normalized probability law, not of an unnormalized weight modulo a gauge volume.
